findings.title: latex-typesetter needs=["rulebook"] but never uses the rulebook grant, so it silently vanishes for a consumer with empty rulebook_sections
locations: catalog/hats/latex-typesetter.toml:6 — persona never references {package.rulebook_sections}; its only 'rulebook' is 'the rendered policy file `latex-idiom.md`'
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:433 — a["hats"] = [... for h in roster if !h["not_applicable"]]
findings.description: resolve_hats() marks a hat not_applicable — and therefore excludes it entirely from the roster — when it needs "rulebook" and cfg.package.rulebook_sections is empty (Preflight.jl:194-195, 210-211). Three of the four hats sharing needs=["rulebook","source"] genuinely consume {package.rulebook_sections} in their persona (doc-policy, naming-policy, invariants-and-decisions), so that gate matches their content. latex-typesetter is the odd one out: its only use of 'rulebook' names the shared, always-rendered policy file latex-idiom.md (part of rulebook_text()'s unconditional POLICY_FILES loop), and it never substitutes {package.rulebook_sections} anywhere. schema/config.schema.json places no minItems on package.rulebook_sections, so a consumer legitimately declaring rulebook_sections = [] is schema-valid — and for that consumer latex-typesetter is silently dropped from every /check-consistency roster even though its whole job (auditing LaTeX idiom against the ever-present latex-idiom.md) has nothing to do with rulebook_sections.
